meta.title: Soufflé: private speech-to-text for macOS
meta.description: Free, open-source dictation and meeting transcription for Mac. Local speech models, French and English, and experimental local meeting summaries.
meta.docsTitle: Soufflé documentation: Mac setup and guides

meta.ogDescription: Free, open-source dictation and meeting transcription for Mac. Local speech models, French and English, and experimental local meeting summaries.

hero.sub: Soufflé dictates into your apps and transcribes meetings on your Mac, with optional experimental summaries. Free and open source, with no account or API key. Text stays local with the default settings.
hero.caption: A live meeting transcript, separating you from everyone else. No virtual audio device, nothing uploaded.
hero.category: Offline dictation and meeting transcription for Mac

features.title: Meeting transcripts: your voice, separated from the others.
features.body: System-audio capture separates Me from Them in the live transcript on a Kyutai model, with no virtual audio device to install. Recording stays hands-off: it notifies you when a calendar meeting begins, notices when the meeting seems over, and picks back up where it left off when your Mac wakes.
bullets: Optional Opus audio with a retention policy, replayable by clicking the transcript
Stop, then Resume later: one meeting can hold several sessions
Recovers or salvages the session if the engine stalls or the mic disappears
Everything grouped by day, searchable by meeting title and dictation text

features.title: Local dictation in your Mac apps.
features.body: With the default model the text streams in while you are still talking, punctuated and capitalised. A local pass can tidy the phrasing before you use it, and that same model handles French and English without you switching anything.
bullets: Text appears as you speak, not once you stop
Press once to start and stop, or hold to talk, including on a lone modifier key
Say a trigger phrase to paste a voice snippet instead of free dictation
Fix a misheard name by hand once, and it stays fixed
A local LLM pass polishes the wording when a provider is available, with editable prompts
French and English on the same model, no switching

features.title: Local summaries and compaction, under evaluation.
features.body: Faithfully summarizing a long meeting remains difficult for a small local model. Soufflé is experimenting with Apple Intelligence, Ollama and LLMLingua-2 compaction across Apple Silicon configurations. A useful transcript comes first; meeting summaries are not presented as a validated feature.
bullets: Summaries and compaction are off by default; opt in under Settings → AI
Fixed target: retain 65% of the text before intermediate long-summary stages

overlay.title: The same dictation, in every app you use.
overlay.body: Soufflé is not a window you type into. Press the shortcut and a small overlay appears above whatever you are in, then the text lands in the field your cursor was already in. Chat, mail, an editor, a terminal: the overlay does not care which, and it is kept out of screen recordings.
bullets: The text lands where your cursor already was, with no copy and paste
Terminals and secure fields can get simulated keystrokes instead
Optional start and stop sounds, so you know the shortcut landed
overlay.caption: Press the shortcut anywhere, talk, and the tidied text lands where your cursor already was.

models.title: Choose your local speech model.
models.sub: All four run locally, downloaded on first use. The two Kyutai models stream text as you speak; the other two transcribe once you stop.

cards.name: Kyutai STT 1B
cards.desc: French and English, streaming as you talk. The one most people should stay on.

cards.name: Kyutai STT 2.6B
cards.desc: English only, streaming, noticeably higher quality if you have the disk and the patience.

cards.name: Whisper Large V3 Turbo
cards.desc: Multilingual and familiar, through whisper.cpp on the GPU. Transcribes once you stop.

cards.name: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3
cards.desc: 25 languages with punctuation and capitalization, fast on the CPU alone. Transcribes once you stop.

owndata.title: Everything stays yours to take with you.
owndata.sub: No proprietary format, no export fee, nothing holding you in.

points.d: One meeting or the whole archive, as ordinary files you can open in anything.
Delete any meeting or dictation from the app. To wipe everything, recorded audio included, quit and delete one folder.
Your transcripts can be searched and read by tools you already use, read-only and on your machine.

owndata.more: Export formats, the MCP server and the command line are in the docs.

docs.title: Soufflé guides for Mac.
docs.intro: Install the app, set up dictation and meetings, then choose the features you need. Each guide covers requirements and settings, including limitations and troubleshooting.

blocks.p: With Homebrew:
Or download the .dmg from the latest release and drag Soufflé into Applications. Every build is signed and notarized, so it opens normally: no right-click detour, no Gatekeeper warning.

On first launch the setup wizard downloads a speech model, between 670 MB and 5.6 GB depending on which one you pick. That download is the only moment Soufflé needs the network in order to transcribe.

table: Mac
Apple Silicon. There is no Intel build.
macOS 13+
Dictation, and meetings recorded from your microphone.
macOS 14.4+

Meetings that also capture the other participants. System-audio capture uses the Core Audio process tap, which does not exist before 14.4. On macOS 13 a meeting still records, and the transcript is labelled Mic only.
Disk
670 MB to 5.6 GB for the speech model, downloaded on first use.
Summaries
Apple Intelligence, which needs macOS 26 or newer, or a local Ollama on any supported version. Transcription needs neither.

blocks.p: The setup wizard has an optional Permissions step; skip it and Soufflé asks for each of these as you use the feature that needs it. Notifications are the exception, requested when the app launches. Settings → System → Permissions shows the current state of each and links straight to the matching System Settings pane.

table: Microphone
Records your voice so it can be transcribed. Needed for everything.
System Audio
Captures what the other participants say, without a virtual audio device. Meetings on macOS 14.4+.
Accessibility

Inserts the text into the app you were using, reads back your corrections after a paste when “Learn from corrections” is on, and installs the native event tap that lets a dictation shortcut bind to a single key (a lone modifier, or F5–F12).
Calendar
Reads today's events to list them on Home and notify you when one starts. Optional, and off until you turn it on.
Notifications
Calendar reminders, a meeting about to stop on its own, a paste that failed. Requested at launch; refusing it only silences those alerts.

blocks.p: Refusing one disables only the feature that needs it. Without System Audio a meeting still records your microphone and the transcript is labelled Mic only. Without Accessibility the dictated text is copied to the clipboard instead of being inserted for you, and a single-key shortcut cannot install its event tap; classic modifier shortcuts still work.

A setup wizard covers the permissions Soufflé needs, which microphone to use (your pick goes to the top of the preference order), the speech model to download, and the dictation shortcut. The default shortcut is <kbd>⌘⇧Space</kbd>.

When a first setup finishes, auto-paste is on if Accessibility is granted: when you stop dictating, the text goes straight into the app you were in. Without it, auto-paste stays off. The shortcut step also has a Launch at login switch, off by default. Everything here can be changed later in Settings.

Press the shortcut anywhere, talk, press it again. The text is inserted into whatever app had focus, or copied to the clipboard while auto-paste is off. Press Esc during a toggle dictation to throw it away. If a paste fails, the text waits on Home under Dictation to recover until you copy or delete it.

Apps that reject a synthetic paste (terminals, secure fields) can receive simulated keystrokes instead. While auto-paste is on, Settings → Interface → Advanced offers three insertion methods: the clipboard and ⌘V, simulated typing, or a direct write to the focused field through Accessibility.

Two passes run on the way out, and each can be turned off. Dictation polish, on by default when a provider is available, sends the raw transcript through a local LLM with an editable prompt template (clean up, professional email, bullet points, remove fillers) and needs Apple Intelligence or Ollama. Learn from corrections, set to Automatic by default, watches the field just after a paste: correct a misheard name by hand and Soufflé keeps that spelling for next time, in the custom dictionary under Settings → Transcription. This needs auto-paste to be on and the paste to succeed. The Suggestions mode asks before adding, and also offers corrections during a meeting.

Voice snippets live under Settings → Transcription: say a trigger phrase at the start of a dictation and Soufflé pastes the expansion instead, case- and accent-insensitive, with no AI polish on that take. The menu bar also offers Copy Last Transcription when you need the previous take back, and Pause Shortcut (1h) when you need the key for something else.
Optional start and stop sounds confirm the shortcut landed.

Both dictation shortcuts are set in Settings → Interface. Each takes a classic combo with a modifier, or a single key (a lone left or right modifier, or F5–F12), which needs the Accessibility permission so the native tap can install. The two bindings cannot share a combination.

table: Toggle dictation
Press once to start, once to stop. <kbd>⌘⇧Space</kbd> by default.
Push-to-talk
Hold to record, release to stop. Not set by default; bind a classic combo or a single key (lone modifier, F5–F12) if you prefer holding.
Cancel
<kbd>Esc</kbd> discards a toggle dictation in progress. It is only captured while one is running.

blocks.p: Dictation does not open a window. A small overlay, the pill, appears above whatever you are working in: a recording dot, the label, a live waveform and a stop button. It stays compact until there is text to show, then widens and grows line by line as you talk.

When you stop, the pill switches to Reformulating… while the local polish pass runs, then disappears as the text lands in the field you were already using. The window is excluded from screen capture, so it does not turn up in the meeting you are in.
You can hide the overlay in Settings → Interface; drag it when visible to move it. Position is remembered across display changes.

A meeting records your microphone and, on macOS 14.4+, the system audio, so the live transcript separates Me from Them as it goes. That separation needs a Kyutai model; Whisper and Parakeet transcribe the meeting as one mixed stream.

The lifecycle is meant to be hands-off: the app notifies you when a calendar meeting begins, and today's events have a start button on Home. It detects when the meeting seems over and stops on its own after warning you, and recovers or salvages the session if the engine stalls or the microphone disappears. When the Mac goes to sleep the recording is closed cleanly, and Soufflé offers to resume it on wake. A stopped meeting can also be picked up by hand with Resume recording, which adds another session to the same meeting. If a microphone stops responding, a banner says so and offers Restart Soufflé.

After 10 minutes without speech, a meeting warns you and stops 2 minutes later unless you cancel, with a 4-hour failsafe behind it. One switch in Settings → Audio turns both off, next to the microphone Soufflé should prefer.

Audio recording is off by default. Turn it on in Settings → System → Data and the meeting sound is kept as compact Opus files, for 7 days, 30 days or until you delete them, replayable with click-to-seek from any line of the transcript. With system audio the file is stereo, you on the left and the others on the right, at about 1.5x the disk of mono.

From a meeting's page you can copy the transcript, export the meeting or delete it. Summary and compaction actions appear after you enable the experimental feature under Settings → AI → Summarization.

This feature is experimental and off by default. Enable Summarization in Settings → AI to reveal provider and model selection, prompt templates, the compaction switch and generation actions in meetings. Turning it off hides those controls while keeping your preferences and saved results. Transcription, exports and read-only MCP access remain available. Dictation polish has its own switch; its AI provider can still be configured when polish is enabled.

Accurately transcribing a meeting locally is already demanding. Producing a faithful summary of a long transcript with a local model is harder still: decisions, conditions, negations, owners and deadlines all need to survive. Soufflé prioritizes a useful transcript across supported Apple Silicon Macs, including modest configurations, rather than assuming everyone owns a large machine.

A meeting of around 15 minutes is generally a more approachable starting point for summary experiments. This is neither an automatic cutoff nor a quality guarantee: speaking density, language and model also matter. Longer meetings introduce more text and relationships to preserve. A Mac with 48 GB or more of unified memory can run larger models and may obtain better results; that hardware should not become a requirement for using Soufflé.

Apple Intelligence's local model has a 4,096-token context window per session, shared by instructions, input and output. A long transcript cannot simply be handed to it in one pass. Models around 7–8B that fit on more Macs have varying context windows: parameter count alone does not determine context size. Even when a model advertises a large window, memory, processing time and faithfulness over long text remain constraints. Soufflé uses intermediate stages for long sources, but those stages can also lose information.

The LLMLingua-2 experiment. Microsoft's llmlingua-2-bert-base-multilingual-cased-meetingbank ranks words to retain fragments of the original transcript. It shortens the input; it does not write a summary or enlarge the summary model's actual context window. The target is fixed: it retains 65% of the text, removing roughly a third of the words. Protected content may increase the retained percentage. A compact saved earlier below 65% shows “A low value omits words.” in its preview until it is regenerated. Compaction can still lose details or relationships, so keep the original transcript as your reference.

One switch, compress long transcripts before summarizing, reduces intermediate-stage input and saves the readable compact text beside the source. It keeps a fixed 65% of the text. Short summaries use the original text and create no compact. You can also generate or regenerate a compact version from a meeting without running a summary. The first download is about 713 MB, followed by local preparation of about 355 MB of fp16 weights. After installation, this processing is local and offline. Editing the source marks an existing compact as stale. Settings → AI also lets you remove the compression model, even with Summarization disabled. Saved compacts and preferences are kept; removal is refused while the model is busy.

Experimental summaries use Apple Intelligence when available on macOS 26 or later, or Ollama. To try Ollama, install the server and download a chat model; availability alone does not establish long-summary quality:

blocks.code:
brew install ollama
brew services start ollama
ollama pull qwen2.5:7b

blocks.p: After enabling Summarization in Settings → AI, leave the server at http://localhost:11434 and select your model. qwen2.5:7b is a starting option offered by the app, not a quality endorsement for long meetings. Edit prompt templates and compare the output with the transcript. The provider is shared with dictation polish, which remains usable without enabling meeting summaries.

With Apple Intelligence or Ollama on localhost, text is processed on your Mac. If you change the address to a remote Ollama server, Soufflé sends it the text needed for summaries or dictation polish. Choose that server accordingly.

Your cloud LLM is another option. Soufflé's local MCP server lets a compatible client read original transcripts even when built-in summaries are disabled. You can use Claude, ChatGPT or another cloud LLM, with an MCP connection appropriate to that client, to produce a more capable summary and feed your second brain. Soufflé ships a local, read-only stdio server; setup depends on the client, and not every client accepts that transport directly. Soufflé supplies no direct integration with those services or automatic cloud synchronization. If you choose this workflow, the external client sends text to your chosen provider and manages your notes under its own settings. See MCP setup.
All models run locally and are downloaded on first use from HuggingFace. Switch at any time in Settings → Transcription.

table: Kyutai STT 1B
Default. French and English, ~2.4 GB, Metal GPU via Candle. Streams text while you speak.
Kyutai STT 2.6B
English only, higher quality, ~5.6 GB. Streams text while you speak. It has no pause detector, so long speech without a quiet gap can lose about 2.5 seconds every 28 seconds.
Whisper Large V3 Turbo
Multilingual, ~1.6 GB, Metal via whisper.cpp. Transcribes once you stop.
Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3
25 languages with punctuation and capitalization, ~670 MB int8, fast CPU inference via ONNX Runtime. Transcribes once you stop.

blocks.p: The two Kyutai models are the streaming ones: text appears while you are still talking. Whisper and Parakeet transcribe the whole recording once you stop, which is fine for a meeting you read afterwards but changes how dictation feels.
A loaded model is unloaded after an hour of inactivity to give the RAM back, and reloaded on the next recording. Change or disable that in Settings → Transcription.
Six tabs. The settings worth knowing about:

table:
Insertion method
Interface › Advanced
Clipboard and ⌘V, simulated typing, or a direct Accessibility write. Change it when an app refuses the paste.

Auto-paste
Interface
On: the text goes into the app you were using. Off, the default: it is copied to the clipboard.

Paste delay
Interface › Advanced
How long to wait before pasting. Raise it if the text lands in the wrong app.

Language and theme
Interface
The interface in French or English, and a light, dark or system appearance.

Dictation sounds
Interface
Start and stop cues.

Hide recording overlay
Interface
Hide the floating HUD while dictating or in a meeting. Drag it when visible to move it; the position is remembered. It never appears in screen captures.

Dictation polish
AI
The local LLM pass and its prompt templates, which you can edit. On by default when Apple Intelligence or Ollama is available.

Custom dictionary
Transcription
Proper nouns and technical terms to spell correctly, filled in by hand or learned from your corrections.

Voice snippets
Transcription
Trigger phrases that expand to a prepared block of text at the start of a dictation. Matching skips the polish pass.

Microphone priority
Audio
An ordered list of preferred inputs and a separate choice for clamshell mode.

Meeting auto-stop
Audio
One switch. On, a meeting stops after 10 minutes without speech, with 2 more minutes to cancel, and after 4 hours at the latest. Off, neither limit applies.

Model unload
Transcription
Free the model's RAM after 5, 15 or 60 idle minutes, or never.

Calendar
Meetings

Off until you turn it on. Lists today's events from the calendars you keep ticked, reminds you a few minutes before one (2 by default), and notifies you when one begins while a call is using the microphone.

Summarization — experimental
AI

Off by default. Enables summary prompt templates, the compression switch and meeting actions. The AI engine card, shared with dictation polish, appears when either is on and shows only the engine in use: Apple Intelligence, or Ollama with its URL and model. Dictation polish remains independent.

Launch at login
System
Open Soufflé automatically when you start your Mac. Off by default; the last step of the setup wizard has the same switch.

Meeting audio
System
Off, keep 7 days, keep 30 days, or keep until you delete it.

Delete downloaded model
Transcription
Deletes the selected speech model from disk. A loaded model is unloaded first; not available while recording. While that model stays selected, Soufflé downloads it again at next launch.

Update check
System

Asks GitHub at launch, then about once a day, whether a newer release exists. Turn it off in About. An update is downloaded only when you press Download update, and installed with Install and restart, which asks you to stop a running meeting first.

blocks.p: The privacy claim is worth checking rather than believing, so here is every outbound connection the app makes.

table: huggingface.co
Downloads your selected speech model on first use. No audio or transcript is sent with that request. Once the model is installed, transcription works offline.
api.github.com

At launch, about once a day, and whenever you press Check for updates, asks whether a newer release exists, and fetches the release notes for What's New. It sends nothing but the request: no identifier, no account, no usage data. Turn the automatic checks off in Settings → System → About.
github.com
Only if you press Download update: fetches the signed update, which is verified before Install and restart is offered.
localhost:11434

Your Ollama instance for summaries and dictation polish. The server receives the text to process. With localhost it stays on this Mac; with a remote address selected in Settings → AI, it goes to that server. Ollama models are downloaded by that instance.

blocks.p: Audio stays on your Mac. Transcripts, notes and summaries are stored in a local SQLite database: Settings → System → Data exports them. Text processing is also local with the default settings. If you configure a remote Ollama instance, that server receives the text used for summaries or dictation polish.
Everything sits in one folder, ~/Library/Application Support/com.souffle.desktop/. Settings → System → Data has a button that reveals it in Finder.

table: souffle.db
SQLite: meetings, transcripts, notes, summaries, dictation history, the custom dictionary and your settings.
models/
Downloaded speech models, filed by engine and backend. Deleting one frees the disk; it is downloaded again if you select that model later, or at the next launch if it stays selected.
recordings/
Meeting audio as Ogg/Opus, one folder per meeting. Empty unless you turned recording on.
logs/
Rotating application logs. This is what to attach when you report a problem.

blocks.p: Backing that folder up backs up everything. Deleting it returns the app to a first launch.

Optional compact transcripts are derived local data stored with their meeting in SQLite and deleted with it. Source edits mark them stale. Compression weights live under models/compression/: approximately 713 MB first download, converted locally to 355 MB fp16. No startup download.

Any meeting exports as Markdown, JSON, or SRT/VTT subtitles, with its recorded audio alongside if you kept any. The whole archive exports as a plain folder of Markdown and JSON. No proprietary container, nothing to migrate out of later.

The bundled souffle-mcp sidecar lets Claude Desktop, Claude Code or any MCP client search and read your meetings and your dictation history. It talks over stdio, opens the database read-only and works even when the app is closed. The server makes no network connection of its own, but the client you connect can send what it reads to its own AI provider, under that client's privacy settings. It takes no arguments. Settings → System → MCP server shows both setup snippets with the path of your installation filled in.

Claude Code. The first command registers the server for you in the current project only. The second registers it in all your projects. Check with claude mcp list or /mcp; remove it with claude mcp remove souffle.

blocks.code:
claude mcp add souffle '/Applications/Soufflé.app/Contents/MacOS/souffle-mcp'

# Or, for all your projects
claude mcp add --scope user souffle -- '/Applications/Soufflé.app/Contents/MacOS/souffle-mcp'

blocks.p: Claude Desktop. In the Claude menu of the macOS menu bar, open Settings…, then Developer → Edit Config. The file is ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json. Add the entry below; if the file already has an mcpServers object, add only souffle to it. Then quit Claude Desktop completely and reopen it. If the server does not appear, read mcp.log and mcp-server-souffle.log in ~/Library/Logs/Claude.

Database. The server reads ~/Library/Application Support/com.souffle.desktop/souffle.db; the sidecar inside the Soufflé Nightly bundle reads the Nightly database. The SOUFFLE_DB environment variable overrides both: set it in an env object next to command in Claude Desktop, or with Claude Code:

blocks.code: claude mcp add --env SOUFFLE_DB=/path/to/souffle.db --transport stdio souffle -- '/Applications/Soufflé.app/Contents/MacOS/souffle-mcp'

blocks.p: Tools. There are five. limit defaults to 20 and is kept between 1 and 200. There is no pagination.

table: list_meetings

Meetings, newest first. All parameters are optional: query, from, to, limit. Returns meetings, each with id, title, started_at, ended_at, is_ongoing, duration_seconds, participants (names), has_summary, has_compact and has_notes.
get_meeting
One meeting. id is required, include is optional. Returns the meeting fields and the requested sections, described below.
search_meetings

Full-text search over meeting transcripts only. query is required, limit optional; a blank query returns nothing. Returns results ranked by relevance, each with id, title, started_at and a snippet where matches are wrapped in ** and cuts marked ....
get_latest_meeting
The meeting that started last. Takes the optional include and returns the same fields as get_meeting.
list_dictations
Dictation history, newest first. Optional limit. Returns entries with id, text and timestamp. No search or date filter.

blocks.p: Search and date parameters.

table: query

FTS5 syntax, applied to transcript text only: titles, notes, summaries and dictations are not searched. Quote a phrase or a hyphenated word, such as "follow-up". In list_meetings a blank value means no filter. A bare term also matches the index's internal type and id fields, so meeting matches every meeting: write content:meeting to match the transcript text only.
from
Earliest start time, inclusive: an ISO 8601 date or date-time, read as UTC without an offset.
to
Latest start time, inclusive. A date alone means midnight at the start of that day, so it leaves out meetings later that day: pass the next day. A date that cannot be parsed matches nothing.
include
Any of transcript, summary, notes, metadata, compact. Omitted or empty means everything; an unknown value is rejected.

blocks.p: Meeting sections. get_meeting always returns id, title, started_at, ended_at, is_ongoing and duration_seconds. The fields below are null when not requested or absent. Use the summary for an overview, the compact for an economical but lossy first pass (check is_stale), and the transcript for exact quotes. list_meetings exposes has_compact.

table: transcript
The edited transcript if you edited it, otherwise paragraphs prefixed with Me: or Them: when the speaker lane is known, without timestamps.
summary, structured_summary
Both selected by summary. The structured one has decisions, action_items (text, owner) and open_questions.
notes
Your meeting notes.
metadata
calendar_event_id, participants (name, email, is_organizer), summary_model, summary_generated_at, segment_count.
compact_transcript
Selected by compact: text, model, rate (share of text it aimed to keep), generated_at, is_stale, source_sha256, approx_tokens (an estimate).

blocks.p: Meeting resource. Each meeting is also a resource, souffle://meeting/{id}. Listing returns the 200 most recent meetings, named by title, without a next page; any meeting id can be read. Reading one returns Markdown with the title, start time, summary, decisions, action items, open questions (each section only when present) and the transcript. Notes and the compact transcript are not included: use get_meeting. No resource templates are advertised.

Ongoing meetings can be read live: ended_at is null and is_ongoing is true. Segments are saved in batches, so the latest ones (up to about 15) may be missing, and newly saved live text is generally not searchable until the session ends.

table: The server exits at startup: Souffle database not found
Launch Soufflé at least once, or fix SOUFFLE_DB.
Every call reports a newer schema version
A newer Soufflé wrote the database. Update the app and restart the MCP client.
Query failed on a search
Invalid FTS5 syntax: quote the terms.
Meeting not found, No meetings found
Unknown id, or no meeting recorded yet.

blocks.p: The souffle binary can transcribe a file, benchmark a model, and summarize or compact a stored meeting without opening the app. It ships inside the app bundle and is not added to your PATH, so invoke it by full path or symlink it once.

blocks.code:
# Run directly
"/Applications/Soufflé.app/Contents/MacOS/souffle" --list-engines

# Or expose it as a `souffle` command
ln -s "/Applications/Soufflé.app/Contents/MacOS/souffle" /usr/local/bin/souffle

blocks.p: It runs headless only when the command line contains one of the six actions below. Anything else opens the app, including a bare souffle --help or an unknown flag on its own. To print the help, add an action: souffle --list-engines --help. There are no subcommands and no --version.

table: --list-engines
List the engine ids and labels.
--list-models
List every engine, model and backend combination with its install status.
--transcribe-file <WAV>
Transcribe a WAV file and print the text.
--summarize-meeting <ID>
Summarize a stored meeting, save the summary with it and print the meeting.
--compact-meeting <ID>
Save and print a compact transcript of a stopped meeting (experimental).
--aec-replay <WAV>

Developer tool for echo cancellation. Replays a lossless stereo float32 48 kHz recording (microphone left, system audio right) and always prints JSON metrics. The app writes such a file only when started with SOUFFLE_AEC_DIAGNOSTIC=1 while meeting audio retention is on.

blocks.p: --compact-meeting and --summarize-meeting cannot be combined with each other or with any other action. --aec-replay cannot be combined with --transcribe-file or a list. If both lists are given, --list-engines wins, and a list takes precedence over --transcribe-file. An option that does not apply to the action is ignored.

Transcription. The WAV must be mono, 16-bit PCM or 32-bit float; any sample rate is resampled. Convert other sources first, for example with ffmpeg -i input.m4a -ac 1 output.wav. The speech model must already be downloaded. The text is the engine's own output, without the app's dictionary or filler filters.

blocks.code:
souffle --list-models --json
souffle --transcribe-file audio.wav
souffle --transcribe-file audio.wav --json
souffle --transcribe-file audio.wav --engine whisper --repeat 5

table: --engine, --model, --backend

Ids from --list-engines and --list-models. Without any of them, the model selected in the app is used (the default model, with a warning, if the settings cannot be read). With any of them, the saved selection is ignored: the engine defaults to kyutai, the model to the engine's first one, the backend to the recommended one.
--repeat N
Transcribe the file N times (default 1, 0 counts as 1). The model loads once and the engine state is reset between runs, so this is a benchmark.
--json
Print JSON instead of text and only log warnings.

blocks.p: Transcription always reads the app's own database: --database and SOUFFLE_DB do not apply to it. With --json it prints one object on one line (wrapped here). profile_source is flags, persisted_settings or default; rtf is audio duration divided by processing time, so higher is faster; with several runs, text comes from the last one.

Meeting actions. Meeting ids come from the MCP tool list_meetings. Both actions are experimental and work whether or not Summarization is enabled in the app. Overrides apply to one run and are not saved.

blocks.code:
souffle --summarize-meeting MEETING_ID
souffle --summarize-meeting MEETING_ID --summary-provider ollama --json
souffle --summarize-meeting MEETING_ID --summary-model qwen2.5:7b --summary-compression on
souffle --compact-meeting MEETING_ID --json
souffle --summarize-meeting MEETING_ID --database /path/to/copy.db

table: --summary-provider auto|apple-intelligence|ollama
Picks the model when --summary-model is absent. auto prefers Apple Intelligence, then Ollama. For Ollama, the saved model if available, otherwise the first one listed. Defaults to the saved choice.
--summary-model <ID>
apple-intelligence or an Ollama model name; the id then decides the provider.
--summary-compression on|off

Overrides the switch that compresses long transcripts before summarizing. It only matters when the transcript needs intermediate stages. A summary never downloads the compression model: without a current compact or an installed model, the original is summarized.
--database <PATH>

Meeting actions only. Without it, SOUFFLE_DB is used, then the app's database. Settings such as the Ollama address and the default summary template come from that database. It is opened for writing: a missing file is created and an older one is migrated, so use a copy if it must not change.
--json
Print the result on one line and only log warnings.

blocks.p: --summarize-meeting prints the saved meeting as JSON (indented without --json). --compact-meeting needs a stopped meeting. It returns the current compact if there is one, otherwise it generates it, downloading the compression model first if missing (about 713 MB). It prints the compact text, or with --json an object with text, model, rate, generated_at, is_stale, source_sha256 and approx_tokens.
Logs and exit codes. Results go to stdout, logs to stderr. SOUFFLE_LOG sets the log filter; the default is souffle=info,warn, or souffle=warn,warn with --json.

table: 0
Success, or help printed.
1
Invalid arguments, a setup problem (unknown profile, model not downloaded, unreadable WAV, model load failure), or a failed meeting action or replay.
2
The transcription itself failed.

blocks.p: Symptom first, then the usual cause.

table: The other participants are missing from the transcript
System-audio capture needs macOS 14.4 or later and the System Audio permission. When it is unavailable the transcript is labelled Mic only and records your microphone alone.
A single-key push-to-talk shortcut does nothing
Lone modifiers and F5–F12 need the Accessibility permission for the native tap. Settings → System → Permissions links there.
The dictated text is not inserted

Auto-paste may be off, in which case the text is waiting on the clipboard. Otherwise it is the Accessibility permission. If Soufflé is already listed and ticked there, the entry can be a stale one left by an update: remove it with the minus button and add it back, or use Repair in Settings → System → Permissions.
One app refuses the paste
Terminals and secure fields often reject a synthetic ⌘V. Switch the insertion method to simulated typing in Settings → Interface → Advanced.
The wrong microphone is picked
Move the microphone you want to the top of the preference order, and pick a separate one for clamshell mode, in Settings → Audio.
Polish or summaries do nothing
Both need a provider. Without Apple Intelligence (macOS 26+), install Ollama and pick a model in Settings → AI. The reason a pass was skipped is shown in the status message and written to the log.
A model download stopped part way
Select the model again to restart the download. Deleting its folder under models/ forces a clean re-download.
Anything else
Settings → System → Data reveals the data folder. logs/ holds the recent logs, which are what an issue needs.

blocks.p: Installed with Homebrew:
Otherwise, drag Soufflé out of Applications.
Either way your data stays. To remove it too, quit Soufflé and delete ~/Library/Application Support/com.souffle.desktop/: meetings, dictations, recorded audio and models all live there.

To reclaim disk without uninstalling, select a speech model you no longer use and delete it under Settings → Transcription → Delete downloaded model, then select the model you want to keep: a deleted model that stays selected is downloaded again at next launch.
The app is Rust with a native Slint interface, plus a little Swift for the overlay. Building it requires an Apple Silicon Mac, Rust, the Xcode command-line tools, and cmake (brew install cmake).

blocks.code:
git clone https://github.com/damione1/souffle.git
cd souffle
make nightly

blocks.p: make nightly builds and opens Soufflé Nightly, a debug build with its own identity that sits next to an installed Soufflé. ./scripts/bundle-macos.sh builds a signed release bundle.
If something does not work the way this documentation describes, open an issue. Include your macOS version, your Mac model, the audio devices involved, and a log from the logs/ folder.

privacy.title: Private by design, not by promise.
privacy.sub: Speech recognition runs on your Mac. Apple Intelligence or a local Ollama also keep summary and dictation-polish text on the machine. A remote Ollama server you choose receives the text sent to it.

points.d: Your audio, transcripts, notes and summaries are stored in a local database you can export or delete. You decide whether a remote Ollama server processes the text.
Once the speech model is on disk, transcription keeps working with the Wi-Fi off, on a plane, anywhere.
No sign-up, no subscription, no API key to paste in. You download it and it works.

privacy.more: Every outbound connection the app makes is listed. See what they are, and why.
